ud6.2:2.1: “Matted-hair ascetics” (_jaṭilā_) were Vedic ascetics practicing bathing and worshiping the sacred flame ([ud1.9]()). | “Jain ascetics” (_nigaṇṭhā_) were followers of Mahāvīra. | “Naked ascetics” (_acelakā_) were apparently also Brahmanical ([mn57]()), although several orders including Jains practiced nakedness. | Some (all?) “one-cloth ascetics” were Jains ([an6.57:4.1]()). | “Wanderers (_paribbājakā_) were homeless religious renunciates—male or female, Brahmanical or other—who wandered seeking alms. | For _khāri_ (“stuff”) see also [sn7.9:14.1]().
ud6.2:4.2: This sentence is phrased as a statement in all editions here, and in the parallel passage at [ud6.2:4.2]() all except the PTS edition, where it is a question. The commentary in both places confirms it is meant as a statement (_“ime arahanto”ti vutte_). Pasenadi is testing the Buddha.
ud6.2:10.4: Commentary: _dhanādiatthāya dhammaṁ na katheyya_, “Don’t teach the Dhamma for the sake of money, etc.”
